# bugs #2997: The return value of an inline __critical function is lost for calls in a nested block

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2997/
- Category: [Trivial fixes](../../fix-trivial.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-2997.patch](../../patches/bugs-2997.patch), commit [`b2510799f`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/b2510799f15b8f28c19bb8491fe1303be8fb7186). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.

```diff
diff --git a/src/SDCCast.c b/src/SDCCast.c
index 394f61a96..4f74c3571 100644
--- a/src/SDCCast.c
+++ b/src/SDCCast.c
@@ -8007,7 +8007,14 @@ expandInlineFuncs (ast * tree, ast * block)
           /* {{inline_function_code}}, retsym                         */
           tree->opval.op = ',';
           if (IFFUNC_ISCRITICAL (func->type))
-            inlinetree = newNode (CRITICAL, inlinetree, NULL);
+            {
+              /* The new node must be at the level of the block it wraps:
+                 fixupInline below takes the base level from it. */
+              ast *body = inlinetree;
+
+              inlinetree = newNode (CRITICAL, body, NULL);
+              copyAstLoc (inlinetree, body);
+            }
           tree->left = inlinetree;
           if (retsym)
               tree->right = newAst_VALUE (symbolVal (retsym));
```

## Finding

When the compiler inlines a `__critical` function at a call inside a nested block, the value that
the function returns is lost, and the compiler issues warning 84 for a temporary variable. The
ticket's program shows both with `-mmcs51`. Its loop calls `cnt_get ()`, and the assembly in the
ticket reads both bytes of `cnt` into A and keeps neither. The cause is in the front end, which
every port uses.

## Cause

`expandInlineFuncs` in `src/SDCCast.c` wraps the copy of the function body in a `CRITICAL` node
when the function is `__critical`. It creates the node with `newNode` and copies no location to
it, so the node has the nesting level that `NestLevel` holds at that moment. For a call inside a
nested block that level differs from the level of the call.

`expandInlineFuncs` then passes the level of the node to `fixupInline`, which derives from it the
level of every node and symbol in the body. `fixupInline` also replaces each `return` by an
assignment to the temporary variable for the return value. With the wrong level, the assignment
refers to a different variable than the one that the call expression reads.

## Fix

`expandInlineFuncs` copies the location of the block to the `CRITICAL` node with `copyAstLoc`. The
block has the location of the call, so `fixupInline` receives the level that it receives for a
function without `__critical`.

## Verification

`tests/bug-2997.c` calls two inline `__critical` functions from nested blocks. Without the patch
all 4 assertions fail. With the patch they pass.
